clue.text: Gets behind remedial action?

parts.note: to be behind something is to support it, to be pro it
cures are actions taken to put an ailment right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a backside is getting corrective treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'behind' as 'in favour of' (PRO) and the whole phrase as 'for cures'.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to obtain it, a plain synonym of gets.

clue.text: Frenchman stifling oath is not someone true to the cause

definitions.text: not someone true to the cause

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the Frenchman's name wraps round the oath

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
egad is a mild old oath

explanation.surface: A Frenchman suppressing a curse is shown up as disloyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' signals one piece smothering another; the oath goes in after the third letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or party, so is exactly someone not loyal to it.

clue.text: Talk to lady, one looking after a big house

definitions.text: one looking after a big house

parts.note: to chat is to talk
Elaine is a woman's name, also a lady of Arthurian legend

explanation.surface: Advice to speak with a woman who manages a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the mistress of a castle or large household, who keeps it running.

clue.text: Withdrawal of certain rot inappropriately written

indicators.note: letters set down in the wrong way are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper retracts something after printing nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriately written' rearranges CERTAIN ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is the withdrawal of a statement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Look at upbringing of boy — it's a disgrace

parts.note: to scan is to look at closely

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing a word up turns it to read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Examining how a boy was raised reveals something shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing of' turns LAD upwards in this down clue, giving DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgraceful affair, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: To change views expediently is neat

definitions.meaning: to adjust one's opinions to suit the times, like trimming sails to the wind

explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer shifts opinion with the political wind, and a trim figure or garden is neat.

clue.text: Equip the man kept under by fool

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man is held down by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept under by' puts HE below CLOT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to provide or furnish them, as in equipping with garments.

clue.text: Like a church festival featuring three men ho men

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Like a church festival featuring three men ho men': the stray 'ho men' is OCR garble (PAT+RON+AL from 'three men') and the scan crop is blank, so the printed clue cannot be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Like a church festival featuring three men ho men

clue.text: Paragon of Roman motherhood, sentimental song writer

parts.note: corn is trite, mawkish material such as a soppy song
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A list identifies an ideal Roman mother as a composer of slushy ballads.
explanation.walkthrough: ELIA is the crossword's favourite essayist, Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornelia, mother of the Gracchi, was held up by Romans as the model mother.

clue.text: Child at home with female, one crawling in the garden?

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
an ant is a small insect crawling about a garden

explanation.surface: A baby is at home with its mother, crawling around outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The crawling child invites a baby; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child.

clue.text: You could see me starring as circus performer

indicators.note: invites the solver to view the letters differently, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A performer boasts of being the star act of the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You could see' rearranges ME STARRING.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster presents the acts in the ring, and is himself part of the circus show.

clue.text: This shout announces delivery

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so what is heard stands for another spelling

parts.note: in cricket each delivery by the bowler is a ball

explanation.surface: A shout heralds a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announces' says a cricket BALL (a bowler's delivery) out loud. The surface's delivery is a baby's.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to shout or cry loudly.

clue.text: Country disc that ought to be hit

definitions.text: Country disc that ought to be hit

parts.words: Country disc that ought to be hit
parts.note: describes the target thrown in a country sport, a disc meant to be shot, while seeming to be a country music record tipped for success

explanation.surface: A country music record deserves to be a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc' and 'hit' suggest a record; the disc is a shooting target in country sports.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay pigeons are discs flung into the air as targets for shooters.

clue.text: She'd appear to be in need of reallocation if this!

definitions.text: She'd appear to be in need of reallocation if this!

indicators.text: to be in need of reallocation
indicators.note: the letters need to be dealt out again, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's figure, if it has gone wrong, needs redistributing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in need of reallocation' rearranges SHE'D APPEAR; whole clue also says that things gone wrong need sorting.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go pear-shaped go badly wrong, and a pear-shaped figure is heavy at the bottom.

clue.text: The Mirror perhaps repeatedly abrasive?

parts.note: a mirror is a looking glass
the Mirror is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid accused of being harsh again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps repeatedly' tells you to use 'The Mirror' twice, once as a glass and once as a paper (the Daily Mirror is a British tabloid).
explanation.definitionFit: Glasspaper is sandpaper, an abrasive sheet for smoothing wood.

clue.text: Shortage here in France is gone over by expert

indicators.note: something gone over is covered, so the skilled word encloses the French one

parts.note: deft means skilful
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A shortfall in France gets checked by an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over by' signals a container: the French word is covered by the word for skilful.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount by which something falls short.

clue.text: Interpret notes, one sounding on organ minute.

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
a cipher is a note sounding continuously on an organ through a fault, and also a nought, something minute

explanation.surface: Notes made about a tiny sound from an organ need explaining.
explanation.walkthrough: CIPHER is an organ fault where a note sounds without its key being pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher is to work out the meaning of something, to interpret it.

clue.text: Act like cutter, touring a lake in ship

indicators.note: touring means going round, so carve goes around the letter

parts.note: to carve is to cut, what a cutter does

explanation.surface: A small boat cuts a path as it travels round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts A inside CARVE. 'Cutter' looks like a boat, but here it is something that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel is a small, fast Spanish or Portuguese sailing ship of the 15th and 16th centuries.

clue.text: Choose to have wealth reduced by half, producing a startling effect

parts.note: to elect is to choose

indicators.note: cutting the word down to half its length leaves its first three of six letters

parts.note: riches means wealth

explanation.surface: Voting to have your fortune halved would come as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by half' cuts RICHES to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric atmosphere or performance is thrilling, giving a jolt like a shock.

clue.text: Break up and go away with school period not quite finished

parts.note: scat is a command to go away

indicators.note: an unfinished word lacks its last letter

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: Children disperse as the term winds down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite finished' drops the last letter of TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter is to disperse or break up in different directions.

clue.text: Astronomer could account for our scenic planet's origin

indicators.note: the letters can be reworked to explain the answer, an invitation to rearrange
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stargazer might explain how our pretty world began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin' takes P from 'planet's', and 'could account for' rearranges it with OUR SCENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Copernicus was the Polish astronomer who placed the sun at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: Minister shown to have sin: no d— saint!

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter named is dropped

parts.note: pride is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A clergyman is exposed as a sinner, no damned saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no d' removes D from PRIDE; the dash makes the surface read as a censored swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Stop something growing?

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow is to stop it
the main stalk of a plant

explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to halt it, and a plant's stalk grows from the ground.

clue.text: Plant in a pot, site needing digging over

indicators.note: soil dug over is turned and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's pot plant needs its bed turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing digging over' rearranges IN A POT SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a plant with red bracts, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Form of love conveyed by the roses

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Love is expressed by a gift of roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is passionate, sexual love, one of the Greek kinds of love.

clue.text: Striking pictures of everyday things in region without work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the area wraps round the work

parts.note: a part is a region, as in parts of the country
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Bold images of ordinary objects come from an area lacking jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense, 'outside', which makes it a container signal. 'Lacking' is the reading it wants you to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art depicts everyday consumer objects in bold, striking images.

clue.text: English stories about wrongdoing in castle

indicators.note: about means around, so the stories enclose the wrongdoing

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: English tales of crime set in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the stories go round the wrongdoing. The castle is the Danish one where Hamlet is set, a fitting place for tales of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the castle at Helsingør in Denmark, setting of Hamlet.

clue.text: Left-wing anger against Court put on a new tack

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A socialist's fury at a court ruling sends things a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: To redirect something is to send it on a new course, setting it on a different tack.
